name: fabflows
description: Routes work from an expensive lead model to tool-scoped workers (explorer and researcher on Haiku, editor and test-runner on Sonnet, refuter and investigator on Opus) and makes the lead re-verify their reports. using-fabflows is the session entrypoint and standing opt-in to fabflows:build, a deterministic loop in which an Opus builder implements a spec and a fresh reviewer returns ACCEPT or REWORK. brainstorming turns a rough idea into that spec: the lead asks bounded rounds of questions with recommended answers, workers read the codebase and the web, and the refuter attacks the draft lens by lens. fabflows-setup points the repository at GitHub Issues, Jira or Linear in a committed .claude/fabflows.json, so specs live in tickets instead of docs/specs/. The ticket skill keeps the ticket current through its MCP tools, and the ticket.js hook requires a Refs trailer on commits, a Spec trailer once the spec is approved, and the key in the PR title; at session start it reminds Claude to close tickets, or ask before cancelling them, whose PR merged or closed outside the session. trace writes an audit trace report outside the repo: each merged change with its PR approvers, ticket, approved spec hash, Compliance section and flags such as no-ticket or self-approved. An ACTIVE guard hook asks before package installs and runners such as npx and denies them in workers, letting through a pypdf install into a literal scratchpad --target with --isolated; it also blocks commits and pushes to a default branch, destructive commands (including ones written into a Makefile, npm script or shell script) and credential-file reads and writes. It fails open: a bug degrades to no guard, never a blocked session.
